findings.title: Copy-paste error: rawTokenId is never null-checked
findings.body: Line 73 reads `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` but should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`. The `grantType` parameter is checked twice (lines 72 and 73), while `rawTokenId` is never validated. A null `rawTokenId` will silently pass construction and cause a NullPointerException later when the token ID is encoded or used.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong substring indices
findings.body: The matcher has two bugs: (1) The condition `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` is inverted — it returns false (mismatch) when the grant shortcut equals the expected value, and returns true (match) when it does not. It should be `!equals`. (2) The substring indices are wrong: the token format is `stttgt:uuid` (positions 0-1 session type, 2-3 token type, 4-5 grant type), so the grant shortcut is at `substring(4, 6)`, not `substring(3, 5)`. Together these bugs make the matcher accept tokens with the wrong grant type and reject tokens with the correct one, rendering all tests using this matcher unreliable.

findings.title: Removal of Context copy constructor is a breaking API change for extensions
findings.body: The `Context(Context context)` copy constructor was removed from `OAuth2GrantType.Context`. This is a public class in `server-spi-private`, which is the SPI layer that extensions compile against. Any third-party extension that was using this copy constructor will fail to compile after upgrading. If this is intentional, it should be documented as a breaking change in release notes.

findings.title: getTokenContextFromTokenId does not handle null input
findings.body: If `encodedTokenId` is null, `encodedTokenId.indexOf(':')` will throw a NullPointerException with no meaningful message. Since this method may be called with token IDs parsed from incoming requests, a defensive null check with a clear error message would be safer.

findings.title: Duplicate shortcut validation does not detect all collision scenarios
findings.body: The check `grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size()` detects when a shortcut is reused across grants (because one map loses an entry) but it does not detect the case where a grant's `getShortcut()` returns the same value as `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.UNKNOWN` ("na"). In that case, the `put` on line 75 silently overwrites the UNKNOWN entry added on line 78, and the sizes remain equal, so no error is raised. The UNKNOWN mapping is then lost, causing `getShortcutByGrantType("na")` to return the colliding grant name instead of "na".

findings.title: Unused import of TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory
findings.body: The import `org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory` is added but never used in this file. The code on line 237 uses `OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE` directly.
